chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him: Is the testimony of people of a different sect/millah permissible for them? He said: 'Yes, if they do not find people of their own sect, the testimony of others is permissible, because it is not fitting that the right of anyone should be lost.'
ai.seo_question: Can people from a different religious sect serve as valid witnesses for another sect in Islamic law?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the testimony of non-Muslims is valid for Muslims when no Muslim witnesses are available, prioritizing the preservation of rights (*dhahab al-haqq*) over strict sectarian exclusivity. This ruling highlights the pragmatic flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding *shahada* (testimony), ensuring that legal proceedings are not stalled by a lack of qualified witnesses within a specific group. It underscores the principle that the integrity of the claim takes precedence when the primary pool of witnesses is exhausted.
